articles.title: Global Market | South Korea’s NPS suspends FX hedging as won hits near two-year high: Reports
articles.content: South Korea’s National Pension Service has suspended foreign exchange hedging as the won strengthened to a near two-year high against the dollar. The move could affect dollar supply and demand in the domestic market, with the pension fund’s large overseas holdings making its currency transactions significant for South Korea’s foreign exchange market.

articles.title: Waterfield Advisors launches two GIFT City funds for global diversification
articles.content: Waterfield Advisors has launched two GIFT City-based outbound AIFs to help Indian family portfolios diversify across global equities, commodities and fixed income. The funds aim to address concentrated domestic exposure and provide access to international markets through India-based vehicles, with the firm recommending a minimum strategic allocation of 10% to global assets.

articles.title: Global Market: China stocks range-bound as tech gains offset bank, insurance sector losses
articles.content: Chinese stocks were largely range-bound on Monday as gains in technology shares offset losses in banks and insurers following Beijing’s $54 billion capital-injection plan. The Shanghai Composite slipped 0.2%, while the CSI300 gained 0.2%. Investors also monitored China-US relations, US rate expectations and semiconductor demand.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan’s Nikkei rallies on semiconductor strength as market volatility eases
articles.content: Japan's Nikkei share average took a leap of over two percent on Monday, propelled by robust performance in chip-related stocks reflecting U.S. semiconductor advances. Investors demonstrated a healthier risk appetite, encouraged by steady bond yields and a firm yen. Both Advantest and Tokyo Electron saw an uptick of more than four percent, while Kokusai Electric impressively skyrocketed eight percent due to its new status in the Nikkei 225 index.

articles.title: Infosys, HCLTech, TCS, other IT stocks drop up to 3% as Fed rate hike worries return. Here's why

articles.title: Did HEG shares really crash 64% in one day? Here’s how the demerger math works
articles.content: HEG shares opened nearly 64% lower on Monday as the stock adjusted for the company’s demerger, which split its businesses into two separately listed entities. The graphite electrodes business will move to HEG Graphite, while the existing listed company will retain advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses and be renamed HEG Advanced Materials.

articles.title: IFCI shares rally 6%, turn multibagger as NSE IPO gets SEBI nod. More upside ahead?
articles.content: IFCI shares rallied 6% after Sebi approved NSE’s much-awaited IPO, clearing a key hurdle for the exchange’s listing. IFCI has indirect exposure to NSE through its majority stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India. The stock has surged over 500% in three years, with analysts seeing further upside.

articles.title: Wires on fire: Why UltraTech’s Rs 1,800 crore Ultravolt bet wiped out Rs 21,500 crore in 2 days
articles.content: UltraTech’s entry into wires and cables triggered a sharp selloff in listed peers as investors assess the impact of intensified competition on market share, pricing and margins. While house wires and light-duty cables face the most immediate pressure, higher-voltage segments remain relatively insulated. Analysts remain positive on long-term industry growth, but caution that elevated valuations leave incumbents vulnerable.

articles.title: BSE shares surge 10% in just 3 sessions. What’s driving the rally?
articles.content: BSE shares extended their winning streak as Sebi announced a review of the methodology used to determine derivative settlement prices following concerns over the new Closing Auction Session. Trading volumes and option activity have declined sharply, particularly at BSE. A consultation paper expected next week could propose changes aimed at reducing expiry-day volatility and improving risk management.

articles.title: Holiday Halt: Why S&P 500, Nasdaq are closed for trading today

articles.title: VA Tech Wabag shares jump 3% after securing repeat order from RIL for ETP project
articles.content: VA Tech Wabag shares rose nearly 3% after securing a medium-sized repeat order from Reliance Industries to design and commission an advanced Effluent Treatment Plant at Jamnagar’s Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex. The project will use advanced chemical, biological and sludge treatment technologies and is scheduled for completion within 13 months.

articles.title: GST reforms rewrote the auto stock map: Who won, who lost and where can investors still make money?
articles.content: The recent GST reforms have significantly impacted the automotive stock market following a rate cut announcement. Notably, Sona BLW Precision Forgings and Samvardhana Motherson International registered impressive growth. Meanwhile, Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor, and Ashok Leyland saw positive movement ahead of their earnings reports. On the downside, stocks like Mahindra & Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki India lagged. Future prospects appear promising, driven by advancements in electric vehicles and fleet modernization.

articles.title: PVR Inox shares crash 8% after alleged Rs 200 crore kickback investigation; senior exec's exit comes to light

articles.title: US Stock Market: Equity funds see second straight week of outflows as investors turn cautious
articles.content: U.S. equity funds saw $11.12 billion in net outflows for a second straight week as rising bond yields, oil prices and Middle East tensions dampened sentiment. Strong AI-related earnings from Nvidia and Dell limited the decline. Investors favored safer assets, with money market funds attracting $48.76 billion, reflecting heightened market caution.

articles.title: Gold prices dip Rs 3,600/10 gram, silver down Rs 6,000/kg as US jobs data lifts rate hike bets; buy, sell or hold?
articles.content: Gold and silver prices remained under pressure as stronger US jobs data raised expectations of higher interest rates. Analysts see both metals in a sideways trend, with key support and resistance levels identified for gold and silver. Investors now await US inflation data and the Federal Reserve’s September meeting for cues on the interest-rate outlook and bullion prices.
